1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.strategy: Strikes at d5 now that Black's ...h6 has spent a tempo, forcing Black to settle the central tension before White has played e4. White gives up the slow plan for a more open fight, with the fianchetto bishop on the long diagonal behind it.

Keeps the centre closed and holds d5 with a second pawn instead of releasing the tension. The bishop stays outside the chain and the dark-squared bishop is freed; Black accepts that White may take on d5 and change the pawn structure.
1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.name: Réti Opening: Anglo-Slav Variation, with g3

1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.strategy: Resolves the tension by taking the pawn. White regains it and the d-file opens, so the queens can come off. Black trades its centre pawn for White's c-pawn and gets a calm, nearly symmetrical game, with the bishop well placed outside the chain.
1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.name: King's Indian Attack, with Bf5
